The Institute for Research on Public Policy (IRPP) is one of Canada’s most trusted and influential think tanks. For more than 50 years, the IRPP has produced evidence-based research, informed dialogue, and practical policy solutions on the issues that matter most to Canadians.

We are seeking an entrepreneurial, strategic, and relationship-focused Director, Development and Strategic Partnerships to lead the Institute’s fundraising, sponsorship, partnership, and revenue-development initiatives. This newly created leadership role offers a unique opportunity to build and grow a diversified revenue portfolio that supports independent public policy research and strengthens the IRPP’s long-term sustainability and impact.

The Director, Development and Strategic Partnerships leads the IRPP’s fundraising and revenue-development activities. Reporting to the Vice-President, Communications and External Relations, and working closely with the President and CEO, executive team, and members of the Board of Directors, the Director will develop and grow support from foundations, major donors, institutional funders, sponsors, and strategic partners while identifying new funding opportunities that advance the Institute’s mission.

PPF thanks itsMission Canadapartner organizations, the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers, Export Development Canada and Deloitte, for their support of this project.

Canada’s Route to More Diversified Trade

The world’s trade winds in recent months have sometimes felt more like a tornado tearing off in unpredictable new directions. The impact has been felt from coast to coast to coast here in Canada, particularly as the basic assumptions of our relationship with the United States — our largest and most tightly integrated trading partner by a wide margin — have shaken and cracked in the gales.

Canadian government and business leaders have been speaking often and in strident tones about the need to diversify our trade portfolio, and the sense of urgency is understandable. To fully comprehend the position Canada finds itself in, however, we need to see the emerging map of this new world clearly.

The upheaval underway goes well beyond a handful of trade relationships. The U.S. is trying to fundamentally reconfigure the global economy, moving away from long-standing commitments to trade liberalization and rules-based trade to a series of often one-sided deals that offer limited stability.

These new U.S. trade policies are causing substantial disruptions that can fundamentally shift economic fortunes for its trading partners. For Canada, they could alter the basic nature of Canadian trade and its economic position in the world.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Public Policy Forum (PPF) --Canada官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Truth and Reconciliation Day: Leave It Better

发布源: Public Policy Forum (PPF) --Canada | 抓取时间: 2026-10-10

What will we leave behind? The National Day for Truth and Reconciliation calls on all Canadians to consider this question, which lies at the centre of the 2026 Action Canada Lecture on Reconciliation and Public Policy.

Delivered in Whitehorse, the lecture by CYFN Grand Chief Math’ieya Alatini presents a vision for northern development that protects the land, strengthens communities, creates lasting opportunity and is founded on trust.

As Canada advances priorities in energy, mining and critical minerals, defence, infrastructure and Arctic sovereignty, Grand Chief Alatini demonstrates why development rests on firmer ground when First Nations hold a meaningful role in determining whether, where and how it proceeds.

She urges policymakers and Canadians to listen closely, to examine the assumptions that shape whose perspectives are heard and acted upon, and to broaden participation in public policy. She affirms that leaving things better than we found them is a shared responsibility.

The Action Canada Lecture on Reconciliation and Public Policy is held annually in memory of Sarah Robinson, a 2014/15 Action Canada Fellow, and in recognition of her commitment to dialogue on Indigenous histories, reconciliation and action.

The Public Policy Forum and Action Canada extend their sincere thanks to Grand Chief Alatini and toYukon Universityfor its partnership and for hosting the lecture on campus.

Howe Institute’s leadership voice, visibility, and scholarly reputation in financial and monetary policy position the Centre uniquely in Canada to build upon its tradition of having real impact that improves Canadian living standards.

The Financial Regulatory Excellence Initiative conducts rigorous and independent assessments of existing and proposed financial sector regulations, identifies regulatory effectiveness and gaps, and promotes a common understanding of optimal regulation.

The Financial Services Research Initiative is a multi-year program organized by the Institute to report and advise on financial sector policy. Its unique work program addresses the economic environment within which financial intermediation takes place, the regulatory environment, and the future of financial intermediation. The Initiative is informed by regular meetings of experts in the sector, policymakers and supporters engaged in the financial services sector, including financial intermediaries, securities market participants and their regulators, among others. The Initiative publishes research by prominent scholars from academia, associations, and the private and public sectors.
